newsitem.title: USA: NHL ICE HOCKEY-LEAGUE REDUCES LIST OF EXPANSION CANDIDATES TO SIX.
newsitem.headline: NHL ICE HOCKEY-LEAGUE REDUCES LIST OF EXPANSION CANDIDATES TO SIX.

text.p: The National Hockey League pared its list of candidates for expansion franchises Wednesday, eliminating five of the 11 groups that made presentations last month in New York.

The Expansion Committee of the NHL Board of Governors said it is still considering applications from Atlanta; Columbus, Ohio; a Houston group headed by Chuck Watson; Minneapolis-St. Paul; Nashville, Tennessee; and Oklahoma City.

The five applicants no longer under consideration are Hamilton, Ontario; Hampton Roads, Virginia; Raleigh-Durham, North Carolina; and two groups from Houston -- one headed by Les Alexander and the other by the Maloff family.
A special subcommittee of the Expansion Committee will further analyse the final six candidates, make on-site visits and conduct further interviews.
"We have a lot of schedules to coordinate," NHL Commissioner Gary Bettman said.

"I have to schedule and form a subcommittee to visit these places. I will probably do that in the next month and visit the sites the following month after that. If we are in a position to expand we will probably announce it before the summer."

Atlanta and Houston are considered the front-runners. The NHL has a history in Atlanta, where the Flames played from 1972-80, before moving to Calgary. The NHL, which is eyeing a more lucrative television contract in two years, is expected to look favourably on the bid by Ted Turner and Time-Warner.

No timetable for expansion has been set and any final approval must come from the Board of Governors. Bettman said in December that the league could add as many as four new teams, but stressed that expansion will not occur before the 1998-99 season.
The fee for new franchises will be at least $75 million, but more likely $80 million, Bettman noted.

The league has expanded by five teams in the 1990s. The San Jose Sharks entered in 1990. The Tampa Bay Lightning and Ottawa Senators began play in 1991 and the Mighty Ducks of Anaheim and Florida Panthers joined the NHL two years later.
